title: Farik Event
description: One record in Farik's append-only log (docs/SPEC.md section 8.5). The envelope says where the event belongs and when it was recorded; kind says what happened and body carries that kind's payload. The pairing of kind and body is checked by the reader, farik_protocol::event::event_from_value, and not here: a schema that pairs them with if and then cannot be turned into Rust types by the generator.

seq.description: The event's place in the log. Assigned by the store on append and never reused. The upper bound is the store's counter's, so that a number past it is refused here, at its own path, rather than by the reader's typing at the root.

recorded_at.description: When the event was recorded, from the injected clock. Never read from the machine's clock by the crate that builds the event.

team_id.description: The team the event belongs to. A blank one is refused by the reader.

project_id.description: The project the event belongs to. A blank one is refused by the reader.

task_id.description: The contract the event is about, when it is about one.

agent_id.description: The agent whose work produced the event, when an agent did.

session_id.description: The session the event was recorded in, when it was recorded in one.

eventBodyWire.title: Event Body Wire
eventBodyWire.description: Every body shape the log holds. The branches have distinct required properties and none accepts an unknown one, so a body matches exactly one. Which one it must be is decided by kind, in the reader.

contractSummary.title: Contract Summary
contractSummary.description: The fields of a contract the board shows, repeated on every event that writes one so that the projections can be rebuilt from the log alone (docs/SPEC.md section 8.4). The vocabularies match task-contract.schema.json, which is the source of truth for them; a test in farik-protocol fails when the two drift.

taskCreatedBody.title: Task Created Body
taskCreatedBody.description: A request was filed as a draft contract (docs/SPEC.md section 5.16 item 1).

created_by.description: The agent id that filed the request, or human.

contractWrittenBody.title: Contract Written Body
contractWrittenBody.description: A contract's content was written or changed.

contractLockedBody.title: Contract Locked Body
contractLockedBody.description: A human took ownership of a contract (docs/SPEC.md section 5.11).

contractUnlockedBody.title: Contract Unlocked Body
contractUnlockedBody.description: A human gave a contract back to the team (docs/SPEC.md section 5.11).

driftDetectedBody.title: Drift Detected Body
driftDetectedBody.description: Reconciliation found the files and the log disagreeing (docs/SPEC.md section 8.4).

projectScannedBody.title: Project Scanned Body
projectScannedBody.description: The project scan read the repository back to the user and proposed criteria for the library (docs/SPEC.md section 5.13).

teamUpdatedBody.title: Team Updated Body
teamUpdatedBody.description: The team file was written. A status change alone is agent.updated.

criteriaUpdatedBody.title: Criteria Updated Body
criteriaUpdatedBody.description: The criterion library was written (docs/SPEC.md section 5.13).

costRecordedBody.title: Cost Recorded Body
costRecordedBody.description: What one session's usage report cost (docs/SPEC.md section 5.5), priced when it was recorded so that a later change to the prices does not rewrite what was charged. The envelope names the session, the agent, and the task when there is one.

unpriced.description: True when no price table in use priced the model: the tokens are recorded, the cost is zero, and no dollar limit counts it (ADR 0015). Left out, as an older log leaves it, the cost was priced.

tokenUsage.title: Token Usage
tokenUsage.description: The tokens one usage report counted. The ceiling is the largest integer JSON holds exactly.

budgetExhaustedBody.title: Budget Exhausted Body
budgetExhaustedBody.description: A budget of docs/SPEC.md section 5.5 ran out, recorded once when it crossed from having room to none. The envelope is the session's that crossed it.

taskStatus.title: Task Status
taskStatus.description: Where a contract is in the lifecycle of docs/SPEC.md section 5.2, the contract schema's own list.

transitionActor.title: Transition Actor
transitionActor.description: Which of the lifecycle's actors asked for a move (docs/SPEC.md section 5.2).

gateId.title: Gate Id
gateId.description: The gate of the row a move took (docs/SPEC.md section 5.2); none for a row with no gate.

blockerWire.title: Blocker Wire
blockerWire.description: What the assignee wrote when it blocked a task: what is in the way and what is needed.

rejectionWire.title: Rejection Wire
rejectionWire.description: What the reviewer wrote when it rejected the work: the criteria that failed and why.

taskTransitionedBody.title: Task Transitioned Body
taskTransitionedBody.description: The governor moved a contract (docs/SPEC.md section 5.2). requested_by is the agent id that asked, or human, or governor; effects are what the decision recorded with the move; assignee, reviewer, and iteration are the contract's after it; blocker, blocker_resolution, and rejection are the evidence the move was judged on, when the requester brought any; reason is the human's words for a move they asked for.

transitionRefusedBody.title: Transition Refused Body
transitionRefusedBody.description: The governor refused to move a contract (docs/SPEC.md section 5.2), with every reason it gave. Nothing else changed.

escalationRaisedBody.title: Escalation Raised Body
escalationRaisedBody.description: A move sent a contract to the human (docs/SPEC.md section 5.7), or an accepted contract's integration could not land (5.14), which moves nothing: the contract stays accepted. detail names the gate that opened the move and, when there are any, the words it was about; for reason integration, what failed in git's or gh's words.

contractEvaluatedBody.title: Contract Evaluated Body
contractEvaluatedBody.description: A contract was held to the Definition of Ready (docs/SPEC.md section 5.3) or of Done (5.4), and whether it passed, with every failure. Recorded before the move or refusal it explains.

contractJudgedBody.title: Contract Judged Body
contractJudgedBody.description: The Scrum Master judged a contract against the Definition of Ready's judgment rules (docs/SPEC.md section 5.3): whether it fits its budget and whether its criteria would detect the failure its intent worries about, with the reason.

criterionRecordedBody.title: Criterion Recorded Body
criterionRecordedBody.description: An exit criterion's result, recorded by the agent that ran it (docs/SPEC.md section 5.4). run_by is the runner's relation to the contract; the Definition of Done reads the latest result per criterion and runner since the task last entered in_progress.

noteWrittenBody.title: Note Written Body
noteWrittenBody.description: A note about the work on a contract (docs/SPEC.md section 5.4): the assignee's completion note, the reviewer's review note, or either's progress note. It does not touch the contract's own notes field.

reviewRecordedBody.title: Review Recorded Body
reviewRecordedBody.description: One verification of a contract summed up (docs/SPEC.md section 5.4), recorded once per verification when the reviewer's session ends and every criterion other than a human one has a reviewer result: criteria_run is how many criteria have one, and passed is whether each one's latest passed. reviewer names the reviewer the verification was about. Nothing gates on it; the metrics read it.

taskIntegratedBody.title: Task Integrated Body
taskIntegratedBody.description: An accepted task's branch reached the integration branch (docs/SPEC.md section 5.14): sha is the integration branch's commit that holds it, into is that branch, and integrated_by is governor for Farik's own merge and human for the human's integrate or a pull request the human merged on the forge.

pullRequestOpenedBody.title: Pull Request Opened Body
pullRequestOpenedBody.description: Farik pushed an accepted task's branch and opened a pull request for it under the pull_request policy (docs/SPEC.md section 5.14): its url, its number on the forge, and the branch it merges.

questionAnsweredBody.title: Question Answered Body
questionAnsweredBody.description: The human answered a question an agent asked (docs/SPEC.md section 5.7): question_id is the sequence number of its question.asked, whose task, when it has one, is on this event's envelope too.

humanAcceptedBody.title: Human Accepted Body
humanAcceptedBody.description: The human approved a contract (subject contract, docs/SPEC.md section 5.16 item 2) or accepted a result (subject result, 5.4), with the words they gave, when they gave any.

escalationResolvedBody.title: Escalation Resolved Body
escalationResolvedBody.description: The human resolved an escalation (docs/SPEC.md section 5.7): the contract moved out of escalated to to, and message is what the next session about it is given.

agentUpdatedBody.title: Agent Updated Body
agentUpdatedBody.description: An agent's status changed in the team file (docs/SPEC.md F1): a paused agent takes no work and its sessions end at their next tool call.

sprintStartedBody.title: Sprint Started Body
sprintStartedBody.description: The human started a sprint (docs/SPEC.md sections 3 and 5.5): its id, what it may spend, null for no budget of its own (ADR 0015), and who started it.

sprintPlannedBody.title: Sprint Planned Body
sprintPlannedBody.description: Tasks were planned into the open sprint (docs/SPEC.md 5.11): by the assigner in its planning session, or by the governor when a task filed under an epic in the sprint joins it.

sprintEndedBody.title: Sprint Ended Body
sprintEndedBody.description: A sprint ended (docs/SPEC.md 5.5): by the governor when every task in it was accepted or cancelled, or by the human. left is the tasks that were in it and were neither, which leave it.

questionAskedBody.title: Question Asked Body
questionAskedBody.description: An agent asked the human a question (docs/SPEC.md section 5.16). The event's sequence number is the question's id. A conversation with no task can ask one, so the envelope names a task only when there is one.

productDocWrittenBody.title: Product Doc Written Body
productDocWrittenBody.description: The Product Manager wrote a product document for an approved epic (docs/SPEC.md section 5.16). path is relative to .farik/product/.

toolCalledBody.title: Tool Called Body
toolCalledBody.description: The PreToolUse hook allowed a tool call (docs/SPEC.md sections 5.6 and 8.2). input is the compact JSON of the call's input, cut to at most 4 KiB, ending in [cut at 4 KiB] when it was cut. The envelope names the session, the agent, and the task when the session has one.

toolDeniedBody.title: Tool Denied Body
toolDeniedBody.description: The PreToolUse hook denied a tool call (docs/SPEC.md sections 5.6 and 8.2). reason starts with the refusal's kind in snake_case, then a colon, then what it says.

toolReturnedBody.title: Tool Returned Body
toolReturnedBody.description: A tool call the hook allowed returned (docs/SPEC.md section 8.2). output is the compact JSON of what it returned, cut to at most 4 KiB, ending in [cut at 4 KiB] when it was cut. A call that failed leaves no tool.returned.

sessionStartedBody.title: Session Started Body
sessionStartedBody.description: A Claude Code session started (docs/SPEC.md sections 8.2 and 8.5): why, on which model, and how hard it thinks. The envelope names the session, the agent, and the task when the session has one; the exact system prompt it was given is kept in .farik/local/sessions/<session_id>/system-prompt.md.

sessionEndedBody.title: Session Ended Body
sessionEndedBody.description: A Claude Code session ended (docs/SPEC.md sections 8.2 and 8.5): completed when the model finished its turn, aborted when its caller stopped it, limit when a limit did, error when the program failed; detail is what the program said about it. The envelope names the session, the agent, and the task when the session has one.
